turn_text: Mr. President, it's been a long day and we thank you and we thank all the senators for their careful attention to the legal arguments and your courtesy to the managers and to the lawyers here. This has been the most bipartisan impeachment in American history and we hope it will continue to be so in the days ahead and nothing could be more bipartisan than the desire to recess. So the only issue before the Senate today, of course, is whether Donald Trump is subject to the court of impeachment that the Senate has convened. We see no need to make any further argument that this body has the power to convict. and to disqualify President Trump for his breathtaking constitutional crime of inciting a violent insurrection against our government. Tomorrow, we will address the amazing array of issues suggested by the thoughtful presentations by our colleagues, including the First Amendment, due process, partisanship under our Constitution, the Bill of Attainer Clause, and many, many more. The meantime, we waive all further arguments. We waive our 33 minutes of rebuttal, and we give those 33 minutes, gratefully, back to the Senate of the United States. All the time you're back, all the time has been yielded back.

assumptions.text: The audience believes that bipartisanship is a desirable quality in legislative proceedings.
The term 'constitutional crime' implies a serious breach of constitutional order that justifies removal from office.
The legitimacy of the impeachment process depends on the perception of fairness and shared responsibility among political parties.
The Senate’s role in impeachment includes both judgment and moral accountability beyond strict legal interpretation.
Recessing is a neutral or positive act that aligns with bipartisan values.
